This section explores the capabilities of Modelica [23], and the Dymola tool [24], to de- velop power system models that are suitable for control system design and analysis. The developed can be further explored to create a more detailed design for specificcontroltasksbeyondthoseforwhichitwasoriginallydeveloped[21]. 2.7.2 SystemModelingandRefactoringforLinearization ThemultimachinepowersystemmodelinthisworkisbuiltusingModelica’sobject-oriented, equation-basedframeworktogetherwithcomponentmodelsfromtheOpenIPSLlibrary. The implementation follows the standard Three-Machine Infinite Bus (ThreeMIB) benchmark system [26], which provides the structural layout and parameters for the generators, net- work, loads, and infinite bus. Each subsystem is represented as an independent, reusable component assembled through Modelica’s graphical interface, which automatically gener- ates the underlying connection equations. The network—comprising busses, transmission lines, transformers, and loads—is constructed as a partial model extending OpenIPSL’s pfComponent structure, allowing the system to be initialized directly from a power-flow solution. Toenablecontrol-orientedanalysis,theoriginalThreeMIBmodelisrefactoredintoalinearization- ready variant in which key internal variables are exposed through explicit input and out- put interfaces. This is achieved by extending the base network model and replacing stan- dard generator and load components with IO-enabled versions that provide RealInput and RealOutput ports. The resulting configuration, shown in Figure 2.22, preserves the full system dynamics while making excitation inputs, PSS signals, terminal voltage, speed, and other relevant quantities accessible for linear model extraction. By linking these IO in- terfaces to their corresponding internal variables, the model can be treated as a structured SISO block, as shown in Figure 2.23, for linear analysis without modifying its physical be- havior. This refactored model, referred to as GridIO, enables Modelica libraries such as Modelica_LinearSystems2 to symbolically derive a consistent state-space representation 30 directly from the same equations used for nonlinear time-domain simulation.
